conventions: The complementizer of the `וְהָיָה` frame is placed on the apodosis waw even where that waw falls in the next verse. DEU.11.13 gives `הָיָה` only *And it shall come to pass*, because the ASV writes no *that* inside verse 13; the *that* of *that I will give* belongs to the waw of `וְנָתַתִּי` at the head of DEU.11.14, where that verse aligns it. DEU.11.29 is the same construction inside one verse, its apodosis waw before `וְנָתַתָּה` taking the *that*. Neither `הָיָה` unit reaches across the boundary and nothing in DEU.11.13 is marked `added` or `unrepresented` on account of the missing word: read each verse's own side of the frame (rule 45).

A relative and its resumptive share one unit wherever the ASV writes a single rendering for the pair, and are split wherever it writes a word for each. This chapter fuses `אֲשֶׁר … שָׁמָּה` → *whither* (11.8, 11.11, 11.29), `אֲשֶׁר … בּוֹ` → *whereon* (11.24), `בָּהּ` → *therein* (11.31), and `אֲשֶׁר … מִשָּׁם` → *from whence* (11.10), that last read as one compound rendering rather than two tokens under rule 30. It splits `אֲשֶׁר תִּדְרְכוּ־בָהּ` → *that ye shall tread upon* (11.25), where the relative holds *that* and the stranded preposition holds *upon*, leaving the resumptive suffix `unrepresented` under rule 22. Count the ASV's words before fusing; the two shapes stand side by side at 11.24 and 11.25.

A preposition standing before a construct noun is fused or split by the number of renderings the ASV writes, and this chapter writes both shapes often enough that the candidate table flags it as a split when it is not one. Fused on one English word: `לִפְנֵי` → *before* (11.26, 11.32), `בִּפְנֵי` → *before* and `עַל־פְּנֵי` → *upon* (11.25), `בְּעֵבֶר` → *beyond* (11.30). Split under rule 2, each morpheme holding a word of its own: `בְּתוֹךְ` → *in the midst* (11.3), `בְּקֶרֶב` → *in the midst* (11.6), `מִלִּפְנֵי` → *from* + *before* (11.23). `עַל־פְּנֵיהֶם` (11.4) is a third case: the ASV writes nothing for the phrase and the single word present, *them*, realizes the suffix, so there is no word to fuse into and both the preposition and the construct noun are `unrepresented`.
report: Checked all 55 multi-treatment lemma groups plus the full dump read end to end (the table is blind to `added` units, so the chapter's four supplied-English calls were checked from the verses themselves). Every bucket treated two ways traces to a difference the ASV wrote and the source licenses; no construction is analysed two ways.

Preposition + construct noun is uniform under rule 30's one-rendering condition: `לִפְנֵי` → *before* (11.26, 11.32), `בִּפְנֵי` → *before* and `עַל־פְּנֵי` → *upon* (11.25), `בְּעֵבֶר` → *beyond* (11.30) fuse on one English word, while `בְּתוֹךְ` → *in the midst* (11.3), `בְּקֶרֶב` → *in the midst* (11.6) and `מִלִּפְנֵי` → *from before* (11.23) spend a word on each morpheme and split. `עַל־פְּנֵיהֶם` (11.4) is neither: the ASV writes nothing for the phrase, and the one word present, *them*, is the suffix's, so both morphemes are correctly unrepresented.

`אֲשֶׁר` + resumptive is fused at 11.8, 11.10, 11.11, 11.24, 11.29 and 11.31 (*whither*, *from whence*, *whereon*, *therein*) and split at 11.25, where the ASV writes *that ... tread upon* — a word for the relative and another for the stranded preposition, the suffix unrepresented under rule 22. All seven large-source-unit review candidates belong to this family plus `כָּל־הַיָּמִים` → *alway* (11.1); each is indivisible on rule 30's subtraction test.

Determiner and article counts are consistent: `הַיּוֹם` → *this day* gives *this* to the article (11.2, 11.8, 11.13, 11.26, 11.27, 11.28, 11.32) while a written demonstrative pronoun takes the phrase's one determiner and leaves both articles unrepresented (11.4, 11.5, 11.22, 11.23); `כֹּל` takes a written *every* (11.6, 11.24) and the article takes *the* only where a second determiner is written (11.8, 11.25, 11.32). Article fronting in construct chains follows the ASV's own rendering — fronted at 11.11 (*of the rain of heaven*), not fronted at 11.12, 11.21 and 11.30 — which is rule 29's count, not a divergence.

Dative `לְ` + suffix is unrepresented wherever the ASV writes a bare English object (11.16, 11.17, 11.21, 11.31) and takes *unto* where the ASV writes one (11.9); the object marker is unrepresented in 37 of 39 places and takes English only at 11.12, where *careth for* reaches its object through a preposition (rule 16's first family). Both differences are ASV-driven.

The one construction that spans a verse boundary is handled correctly on both sides: DEU.11.13's `וְהָיָה` keeps only *And it shall come to pass*, and the *that* of its frame is taken by the apodosis waw of `וְנָתַתִּי` in DEU.11.14; DEU.11.29 is the same construction inside one verse. Recorded as a convention, since it is invisible from inside 11.13.

The four `added` units are each licensed by a named rule and none is a fold-avoidance: *I speak* (11.2, a whole supplied clause, rule 20), *your* (11.9, no possessive morpheme, rule 18), *it* (11.10, supplied object with no object morpheme, rule 44), italic *and* (11.11, coordinator for a clause with no waw in it, rule 14).

BSB: none of the 33 disagreements is a genuine error. The Td (18), R (6) and To (5) classes are the documented convention differences — articles the ASV does not write, prepositions the ASV's recasting leaves nothing to say, and H853. The four singletons are the same: `פְּנֵי` (11.4) is in a phrase the ASV renders only by its suffix; `הִוא` (11.10) is a resumptive subject the ASV does not separately write; `ן` (11.22) is a paragogic nun, unrepresented by rule 32; `הּ` (11.25) is a resumptive suffix under rule 22. Nothing was changed to move the rate.

Left standing after review: `פַּחְדְּכֶם וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם` → *the fear of you and the dread of you* (11.25) is aligned in the Hebrew's order, though the crossed reading (`פַּחַד` → *dread*, `מוֹרָא` → *fear*) is the lexically more direct one. The verse names the competing reading under rule 8, no other verse in the chapter writes either lemma, and reopening a documented intra-verse tie with no cross-verse evidence is not this pass's work.
